solutions.title: Two pointers (slow/fast)
solutions.description:
**Approach:** `write` stays at the last unique; `read` scans ahead; copy when values differ.

**Why preferred:** No shifting; returns the new length as required.

**Example walkthrough:** Write pointer stays on the last unique. Read finds `2` different from `1`, writes it next, and returns write+1 = `2`.

solutions.title: In-place splice duplicates
solutions.notes: splice each duplicate — correct but O(n²)
solutions.description:
**Approach:** Walk with index `i`; when `nums[i] === nums[i-1]`, `splice(i, 1)` and stay; else advance.

**vs recommended:** Logic is clear. Interview target is the slow/fast write pointer so each element moves at most once.

**Example walkthrough:** When you see a duplicate next to the previous value, `splice` it out; after removing the second `1`, the array is `[1, 2]`.
